key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameters should be tuned to minimize coating defects, with service humidity considered when assessing wear performance.
method: Deposited Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examined droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Tested corrosion and tribological behavior under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links greater porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate with increasing humidity.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance ranges, and the reported humidity-dependent wear involves Si3N4 counterfaces.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
